title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on How to Handle Petitions for Cases Sentenced before the "Cultural Revolution"

articles.content_en: I. Where a party to a criminal case adjudicated before the "Cultural Revolution" files a petition, or a relevant unit requests a review, or judicial personnel themselves discover a possible error and propose a review, the People's Court shall, as a regular task, conscientiously examine and handle the matter. However, no comprehensive review shall be conducted for criminal cases adjudicated before the "Cultural Revolution."

II. In handling petitions regarding criminal cases adjudicated before the "Cultural Revolution," except where the Central Committee has made specific provisions since the Third Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China for resolving historical legacy issues, which shall be reviewed and corrected in accordance with such provisions, for other petition cases, the appropriateness of the original judgment shall be measured according to the Central Committee's policies and national laws in force at the time of the judgment, and the present policies and laws shall not be applied to cases adjudicated in the past.

III. For specific cases, if the main facts or basic nature are wrongly determined, or if a conviction and sentence are imposed for acts that, according to the Central Committee's policies and national laws at the time, did not constitute a crime and should not have been sentenced, the judgment shall be altered and corrected. If the main facts or basic nature are not erroneous, generally the judgment may not be altered. Where the sentence is manifestly excessive and the person is still serving the sentence, the judgment may be altered as appropriate; if the sentence has already been fully served, generally the judgment may no longer be altered.

IV. Where a petition is filed with the original trial People's Court, it shall be handled by the original trial People's Court; where a petition is filed with a higher People's Court, it may generally be referred to the original trial People's Court for handling. For major or difficult cases, or cases where repeated petitions have been filed with good cause yet have not been properly handled, the case may be handled by the next higher People's Court or the Higher People's Court.
For petitions concerning cases adjudicated by the former branch courts of the Supreme People's Court, the relevant Higher People's Court shall be entrusted to ascertain the facts and submit its proposed handling opinion, after which the matter shall be handled by the Supreme People's Court.

V. For the follow-up work after the alteration of judgments in wrongly decided cases, reference shall be made to the provisions of Document No. 96 of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China in 1979. Practical issues in the follow-up work after the alteration and correction of judgments shall be primarily resolved at the grassroots level; for cases where the judgment is altered by a higher People's Court, the court may entrust the People's Court at the location of the party concerned or the relevant People's Court to assist in handling.
The handling of petitions concerning criminal cases adjudicated before the "Cultural Revolution" shall be approached with caution. When major issues or other difficult problems arise, the matter shall be reported to the Party committee for resolution.
